Recommendation: Maintain current contact details
Evidence method used: Manual inspection and inquiry
Technical observation and root cause: Primary contact name, address, telephone and email are current in all three accounts and match the company register (verified with the CEO).
Evidence inspected: Account settings screenshots for all 3 accounts, 13 Oct 2026; inquiry of the CEO.
Core remediation directive: Keep. Re-confirm at each quarterly assessment.

Recommendation: Ensure security contact information is registered
Evidence method used: Security Hub CSPM (production) + read-only CLI (other accounts)
Technical observation and root cause: No security alternate contact is registered in any account. CloudCo security and abuse notices (for example exposed-key alerts) go to the founder's billing mailbox, which nobody in IT monitors.
Evidence inspected: Security Hub Account.1 FAILED (production); CLI for management and staging.
Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-005 s5.2 reporting channels (not extended to the cloud provider)
Core remediation directive: Register a monitored security@ distribution list as the security contact in all three accounts.

Recommendation: Ensure no 'root' user account access key exists
Evidence method used: Security Hub CSPM (production) + read-only CLI (other accounts)
Technical observation and root cause: No root access key exists in any account.
Evidence inspected: Security Hub IAM.4 PASSED (production); credential reports for all 3 accounts.
Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-002 s4.4.3
Core remediation directive: Keep. Add an SCP or alert that flags any root access key creation.

Recommendation: Ensure MFA is enabled for the 'root' user account
Evidence method used: Security Hub CSPM (production) + read-only CLI (other accounts)
Technical observation and root cause: MFA is active on all three root users. All three devices are virtual (an authenticator app), which satisfies 1.4 but not CGI-POL-002 s4.4.3 or recommendation 1.5. A PASS here is one day's setting, not evidence that root use is restricted.
Evidence inspected: Security Hub IAM.9 PASSED (production); credential reports for all 3 accounts (mfa_active = true).
Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-002 s4.4.3
Core remediation directive: Keep, and upgrade to hardware MFA under 1.5.

Recommendation: Ensure hardware MFA is enabled for the 'root' user account
Profile reason: CGI-POL-002 s4.4.3 requires a hardware MFA device on the CloudCo root user
Evidence method used: Security Hub CSPM (production) + read-only CLI (other accounts)
Technical observation and root cause: No hardware MFA device is registered for any root user. CGI-POL-002 s4.4.3 requires one, so this Level 2 recommendation is mandatory for Cypher. The policy is stricter than the Level 1 profile.
Evidence inspected: Security Hub IAM.6 FAILED (production); the root MFA serial appears in the virtual MFA device list in all 3 accounts.
Audit command or console path: aws iam list-virtual-mfa-devices  (root serial listed = virtual, not hardware)
Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-002 s4.4.3
Core remediation directive: Register two FIDO hardware keys per root user (one in the CTO's custody, one in the office safe). Until then, operate proposed exception EXC-004 with a root-login alert.

Recommendation: Eliminate use of the 'root' user for administrative and daily tasks
Evidence method used: Manual inspection and inquiry
Technical observation and root cause: The management-account root user signed in 4 times in the last 90 days to download invoices and update the payment card. None of the four uses was documented and no alert fired, so CGI-POL-002 s4.4.3 was breached twice per use. Root credentials sit in the CTO's personal password vault, not sealed.
Evidence inspected: Credential report (password_last_used); CloudTrail ConsoleLogin events with userIdentity.type = Root in the management account; inquiry of the CTO.
Audit command or console path: aws iam get-credential-report; CloudTrail lookup-events for ConsoleLogin by Root
Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-002 s4.4.3
Core remediation directive: Turn on IAM access to Billing and give Finance a billing role; seal root credentials; document every root use.

Recommendation: Ensure IAM password policy requires minimum length of 14 or greater
Evidence method used: Security Hub CSPM (production) + read-only CLI (other accounts)
Technical observation and root cause: Minimum length is 8 in all three accounts. CGI-POL-002 s4.1.1 requires 14 and s4.1.2 requires 16 for privileged accounts, and every CloudCo console user is privileged.
Evidence inspected: Security Hub IAM.15 FAILED (production); CLI for management and staging.
Core remediation directive: Set minimum length to 16 now. The rule becomes moot once console access is federated (CF-09).

Recommendation: Ensure IAM password policy prevents password reuse
Evidence method used: Security Hub CSPM (production) + read-only CLI (other accounts)
Technical observation and root cause: Password reuse prevention is not set in any account.
Evidence inspected: Security Hub IAM.16 FAILED (production); CLI for management and staging.
Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-002 s4.1
Core remediation directive: Set PasswordReusePrevention to 24.

Recommendation: Ensure MFA is enabled for all IAM users that have a console password
Evidence method used: Security Hub CSPM (production) + read-only CLI (other accounts)
Technical observation and root cause: 7 of 8 console users have MFA. The eighth, ext-ops-contractor, has none. All 7 MFA devices are authenticator-app codes, contrary to CGI-POL-002 s4.3.3 (phishing-resistant factor for privileged accounts). CIS cannot see the factor type, so a CIS PASS would still have been a policy FAIL.
Evidence inspected: Security Hub IAM.5 FAILED (production); credential report; list-mfa-devices per user.
Audit command or console path: aws iam get-credential-report  (password_enabled = true AND mfa_active = false)
Core remediation directive: Disable ext-ops-contractor today; move admins to FIDO2 keys through federated access (CF-09).

Recommendation: Do not create access keys during initial setup for IAM users with a console password
Evidence method used: Manual inspection and inquiry
Technical observation and root cause: ext-ops-contractor was given a console password and an access key on the same day (14 Mar 2025). The key has never been used.
Evidence inspected: Credential report: user_creation_time equals access_key_1_last_rotated; access_key_1_last_used_date = N/A.
Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-003 s4.3.4 (provision only what the approved ticket grants)
Core remediation directive: Delete the key. Issue programmatic access only through roles.

Recommendation: Ensure credentials unused for 45 days or more are disabled
Evidence method used: Security Hub CSPM (production) + read-only CLI (other accounts)
Technical observation and root cause: ext-ops-contractor last signed in on 02 Apr 2025, 562 days ago. Password and key are both still active. The contractor's engagement ended in April 2025 and no leaver ticket exists.
Evidence inspected: Security Hub IAM.22 FAILED (production); credential report.
Core remediation directive: Disable the user today; run the monthly orphaned-account reconciliation in CGI-POL-003 s4.7.3 for CloudCo too.

Recommendation: Ensure there is only one active access key for any single IAM user
Evidence method used: Read-only CLI (SecurityAudit role)
Technical observation and root cause: No user holds two active keys.
Evidence inspected: list-access-keys for all 9 users (CIS 'Automated', but no Security Hub control - checked by CLI).
Core remediation directive: Keep.

Recommendation: Ensure access keys are rotated every 90 days or less
Evidence method used: Security Hub CSPM (production) + read-only CLI (other accounts)
Technical observation and root cause: Two keys exceed 90 days: codeco-deploy (412 days, used daily by the CodeCo deployment pipeline) and ext-ops-contractor (581 days, never used).
Evidence inspected: Security Hub IAM.3 FAILED (production); credential report access_key_1_last_rotated.
Drawer 1 policy reference: None for machine credentials - CGI-POL-002 covers people only
Core remediation directive: Replace codeco-deploy with OpenID Connect federation from CodeCo to an IAM role; delete both keys.

Recommendation: Ensure IAM users receive permissions only through groups
Evidence method used: Security Hub CSPM (production) + read-only CLI (other accounts)
Technical observation and root cause: Two users have policies attached directly: ext-ops-contractor (cgi-ops-fullaccess) and codeco-deploy (cgi-deploy).
Evidence inspected: Security Hub IAM.2 FAILED (production).
Audit command or console path: aws iam list-attached-user-policies; aws iam list-user-policies
Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-003 s4.2.1 role profiles
Core remediation directive: Grant all human access through Identity Center permission sets (CF-09) and machine access through roles.

Recommendation: Ensure IAM policies that allow full '*:*' administrative privileges are not attached
Evidence method used: Read-only CLI (SecurityAudit role)
Technical observation and root cause: cgi-ops-fullaccess allows Action '*' on Resource '*'. It is attached to the Engineering-Admins group (4 users) and to ext-ops-contractor. Nobody uses a separate administrative account (CGI-POL-002 s4.4.1).
Evidence inspected: list-policies --only-attached --scope Local, then get-policy-version (CIS 'Automated', no Security Hub control in the v5.0.0 standard).
Audit command or console path: aws iam list-policies --only-attached --scope Local; aws iam get-policy-version
Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-002 s4.4.1; CGI-POL-003 s4.2.1
Core remediation directive: Detach and delete cgi-ops-fullaccess; give admin rights only through a time-bound elevated permission set.

Recommendation: Ensure a support role has been created to manage incidents with AWS Support

Evidence inspected: Security Hub IAM.18 FAILED (production); CLI for management and staging.

Evidence inspected: Security Hub IAM.26 PASSED (production).
Core remediation directive: Keep.

Recommendation: Ensure that IAM External Access Analyzer is enabled for all regions
Evidence method used: Security Hub CSPM (production) + read-only CLI (other accounts)

Profile reason: Level 2 - advisory, reported but not scored

Technical observation and root cause: Each account has its own IAM users. Evidence inspected: Inspection: no IAM Identity Center instance, no SAML or OIDC identity provider configured; inquiry of the IT Operations Manager.
Audit command or console path: aws sso-admin list-instances; aws iam list-saml-providers
Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-003 s4.5.2 four-hour revocation

Evidence inspected: Security Hub IAM.27 PASSED (production).
Core remediation directive: Keep.

Recommendation: Ensure S3 Bucket Policy is set to deny HTTP requests
Profile reason: Level 2 - advisory, reported but not scored
Evidence method used: Security Hub CSPM (production) + read-only CLI (other accounts)
Technical observation and root cause: No bucket policy denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false. Clients appear to use TLS in practice, but nothing enforces it.
Evidence inspected: Security Hub S3.5 FAILED on 5 of 5 buckets.
Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-004 s4.2 (encryption in transit for Confidential and Restricted)
Core remediation directive: Add a Deny statement on aws:SecureTransport = false to every bucket policy.

Recommendation: Ensure MFA Delete is enabled on S3 buckets
Profile reason: Level 2 - advisory, reported but not scored
Evidence method used: Security Hub CSPM (production) + read-only CLI (other accounts)
Technical observation and root cause: Versioning is on for cgi-prod-exports and cgi-prod-app-attachments; MFA Delete is on for none. Only the root user can enable MFA Delete, which conflicts with 1.6 (see RC-07).
Evidence inspected: Security Hub S3.20 FAILED.
Core remediation directive: Use S3 Object Lock (governance mode) on the log archive and Restricted buckets instead, and record that choice as the Cypher deviation from 2.1.2.

Recommendation: Ensure all data in Amazon S3 has been discovered, classified, and secured when necessary
Profile reason: Level 2 - advisory, reported but not scored
Evidence method used: Manual inspection and inquiry
Technical observation and root cause: No data discovery has ever run and no bucket carries a classification tag. Manual listing found a full 2024 customer database export in cgi-data-migration-2024 (Restricted under CGI-POL-004 s4.1.3), outside every approved system.
Evidence inspected: Macie not enabled; manual object listing of all 5 buckets on 14 Oct 2026; inquiry of the CTO.
Audit command or console path: aws macie2 get-macie-session; aws s3api list-objects-v2
Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-004 s4.1.3; s4.2 named approved systems
Core remediation directive: Run a one-off sensitive-data discovery job on all buckets; tag buckets with the CGI-POL-004 tier; feed the result into the REC-05 asset inventory.

Recommendation: Ensure that S3 is configured with 'Block Public Access' enabled
Evidence method used: Security Hub CSPM (production) + read-only CLI (other accounts)
Platform asset and service: S3 - account-level Block Public Access; 5 buckets
Technical observation and root cause: Account-level Block Public Access is OFF (all four settings false) since 22 Feb 2024, when it was switched off to publish cgi-www-assets (website images and CSS). Bucket-level BPA is on for 3 buckets and off for cgi-www-assets (public by design) and cgi-data-migration-2024 (switched off 11 Jun 2024 to grant a consultant cross-account access, CF-03). No SCP stops anyone changing it.
Evidence inspected: Security Hub S3.1 FAILED (account); S3.8 FAILED on 2 of 5 buckets; CloudTrail PutAccountPublicAccessBlock event 22 Feb 2024.
Audit command or console path: aws s3control get-public-access-block --account-id <id>; aws s3api get-public-access-block --bucket <bucket>
Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-004 s4.2 Handling Matrix
Core remediation directive: Front cgi-www-assets with CloudFront and Origin Access Control, then turn on all four account-level settings and protect them with an SCP.

Recommendation: Ensure that encryption-at-rest is enabled for RDS instances
Evidence method used: Security Hub CSPM (production) + read-only CLI (other accounts)
Technical observation and root cause: Storage is encrypted with the CloudCo-managed key aws/rds. CIS is satisfied. CUEC 4 asks for key management by Cypher, which a provider-managed key does not show (see CF-05).
Evidence inspected: Security Hub RDS.3 PASSED.
Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-004 s4.2
Core remediation directive: Keep. Move to a customer-managed key at the next major-version upgrade.

Recommendation: Ensure the Auto Minor Version Upgrade feature is enabled for RDS instances
Evidence method used: Security Hub CSPM (production) + read-only CLI (other accounts)
Technical observation and root cause: Auto minor version upgrade is off. Minor versions are applied by hand, and the last one was applied 7 months ago.
Evidence inspected: Security Hub RDS.13 FAILED.
Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-001 s4.4.3 (14-day patching - written for workstations, not platforms)
Core remediation directive: Enable auto minor version upgrade inside the agreed maintenance window.

Recommendation: Ensure that RDS instances are not publicly accessible

Evidence inspected: Security Hub RDS.2 PASSED.
Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-004 s4.2

Recommendation: Ensure Multi-AZ deployments are used for enhanced availability in Amazon RDS

Drawer 1 policy reference: CGI-POL-001 s4.2.3 (no degrading of logging - but no rule requires logging to exist)

Drawer 1 policy reference: None - no cloud configuration standard exists (CG-03)
